scope: Creative AI weekly edition, October 13–19 Toronto. No widening needed. Original publication dates retained; ResStreamGS and Instant Soundtracks carried from the midweek delta, with no new launch implied. SOTA claims are scoped author/vendor results, not independent rankings. No robotics or physical AI.

papers.title: ResStreamGS: stop sending the whole scene every frame.
papers.full_title: ResStreamGS: Residual-Sensitive Dual-Stream Gaussian Splatting for Mobile Volumetric Video Streaming
papers.summary: Caches stable splats per frame group; updates attribute-sensitive splats frame by frame.
papers.change: October 15 v1, covered in the October 16 delta and carried into this weekly synthesis with a new original interactive. Not a new October 19 release.
papers.evaluation: Author tests: six 300-frame sequences, held-out cameras, 20-frame groups. Against a controlled V3-style baseline: +7.51–8.35 dB PSNR and 21.4–56.5% lower amortized payload. 30.883 FPS on one Snapdragon 778G phone.
papers.caveat: Payload is not wireless performance. Culling and pruning also improve speed. Abrupt changes challenge fixed groups; GIFStream has smaller payloads.
papers.access: Full paper reviewed; implementation not verified, no reproduction.
papers.creator_implication: For captured volumetric scenes. Stationary splats can still need appearance updates.
papers.review_depth: Primary methods, evaluation, ablations and submission history.

papers.title: TriFold: give irregular Gaussian scenes a regular latent space
papers.full_title: TriFold: Folding irregular 3D Gaussians into structured latents for 3D Scene Generation
papers.summary: A native Gaussian VAE maps variable-size scenes to triplane latents. Multiple learned slots preserve information when primitives collide in a projected cell; occupancy and set decoding recover adaptive local counts. A latent flow model supports point-cloud or single-image conditioning.
papers.change: New to the archive this week. Original submission October 16; an October 19 aggregator date is not a revision.
papers.evaluation: Author tests on InteriorGS and Aria/SceneSplat: approximately 19,600 crops plus 8,600 scenes, split before cropping. Reconstruction reports 26.55 dB PSNR versus GaussianGPT's 21.40 under the adapted common protocol. Generation is assessed within its own conditioning setup, without a matched cross-generator comparison.
papers.caveat: Limited indoor-scene diversity and fixed physical crop scale constrain generalization. Unseen areas are plausible completions, not recovered truth. The local candidate count remains bounded; adaptive does not mean unlimited.
papers.access: Paper available. Official project page retrieval failed; code, weights and license availability not verified.
papers.creator_implication: Relevant to generating explorable 3D set pieces from partial views, with a clear distinction between observed and invented geometry.
papers.review_depth: Primary full method, evaluation, appendix limitations; no execution

papers.title: MOSS-Image: give the renderer a layout
papers.summary: A 5B DiT combines text and layout conditioning with an optional external prompt planner. Structured boxes make composition an explicit input.
papers.change: Official repository dates Base/SFT code-and-weight release October 16. Paper v1 was submitted October 16; the repository's October 19 news entry announces arXiv availability, not a separate new model release.
papers.evaluation: Authors report 96.3 Mean-6 on LLTB: 240 English/Chinese text tasks, four images each, all scored. The OCR multiset-recall metric ignores order and does not directly penalize extra text. RLA uses 61 design tasks and blind human preferences; MOSS ranks second among displayed end-to-end systems with an external planner. These are author-run evaluations, not an independent reproduction.
papers.caveat: Current backbone is text-to-image, with no direct reference-image conditioning or image editing. Layout changes regenerate an image. The external planner can introduce factual/design errors. General superiority and reliable typesetting are unestablished.
papers.access: Public Base/SFT weights and inference code verified; SFT model card explicitly licenses weights and bundled inference code Apache-2.0. No generation run. Official defaults: 50 Euler steps, CFG 3, shift 5, negative-branch layer 22 skipping; 5B excludes the separate frozen 9B text encoder.
papers.creator_implication: A practical candidate for editable poster/storyboard layout specifications. Review the rendered wording, not just visual appeal or OCR coverage.
papers.controls: Drag colored text/object boxes; edit exact strings and line breaks; change canvas ratio; toggle centered-pixel versus normalized coordinate display. Show bbox conversion and overlap, not invented generated outputs.
papers.misconception: A high text-coverage score means every string is correct and in the right order.
papers.visual_status: Proposed analytic layout/metric explainer; no MOSS inference built or run.
papers.review_depth: Read primary history, method, evaluation and limitations, plus evaluation appendix, official guide and SFT card.

papers.version: October 15 launch; base and distilled checkpoints
papers.title: FLUX 3 Image Klein: a box is a guide, not a mask.
papers.summary: BFL releases a 5.6B image transformer with generation, editing and up to ten references. A 50-step base and 16-step distilled checkpoint expose bounding-box layout control.
papers.change: October 15 launch, newly added to this weekly review; exact later checkpoint revisions were not verified.
papers.evaluation: Vendor internal preference evaluations cover generation, editing and multi-reference tasks. NVIDIA reports 1 MP GPU timing; API comparisons time BFL server-side and competitors client-side. No independent reproduction here.
papers.caveat: Boxes guide placement and scale, not hard masks; edits may affect other regions. API pixel restoration is a separate feature. Generator parameter count excludes the text encoder and prompt upsampler; headline 8 GB operation is configuration-specific.
papers.access: Public reference code and gated base/distilled HF repositories verified. FLUX Kommunity terms include a qualifying commercial-output exception below US$5M annualized revenue; not unrestricted commercial fine-tuning/distribution. No weights downloaded or inference run.
papers.creator_implication: Useful for local layout-controlled edits and adaptation. Supply expanded scene captions and budget the whole pipeline, not just transformer weights.
papers.review_depth: Launch, both model cards, reference README and API specification inspected. Model history pages failed; no execution.

papers.title: Instant Soundtracks: keep music and effects editable.
papers.summary: Video-conditioned music and timed effects arrive with separate editable tracks and optional reference to the video's existing audio.
papers.change: October 15 release, carried into the weekly list from October 16's delta. Article updated October 19; no second launch inferred.
papers.evaluation: Official feature announcement and API contract, with no quantitative synchronization benchmark or independent output test in this review.
papers.caveat: Detection of a visual event does not guarantee perfect audio timing. API add_sfx, separate_tracks and use_audio_as_reference all default false; enabling separate tracks returns a ZIP.
papers.access: Vendor says available in ElevenCreative, ElevenMusic and API. API accepts up to ten videos, 200 MB and 600 seconds combined. No paid request or generation run.
papers.creator_implication: Score an assembled edit, then correct effects or swap music without remaking the video. Compare event timing and sound quality separately.
papers.review_depth: Launch publication/update dates, current product listing and API flags/limits verified.

papers.title: Mirelo SFX 2.0: keep the take, rebuild the sound.
papers.summary: Video-to-sound generation replaces unwanted audio with Foley and ambience across cuts, while retaining the spoken performance.
papers.change: October 14 launch, newly discovered in this review; Runway MCP integration is dated October 15.
papers.evaluation: Vendor blind test: 25 screened raters judged 30 videos per comparison. Against Seedance 2.5 native audio: 47% preferred Mirelo, 28% native, 25% ties. The 72% headline includes ties.
papers.caveat: The FAQ says speech is regenerated, not guaranteed waveform-preserved. Tests are vendor-run and scoped to selected clips. A separately controlled stem variant is still coming soon.
papers.access: Studio, API, MCP and selected partner access announced; up to ten-minute edits in Studio/API. Weights not verified; no listening or generation test.
papers.creator_implication: A finishing pass for an assembled scene; audition dialogue fidelity and ambience continuity before replacing the source audio.
papers.review_depth: Primary launch, evaluation protocol, availability and FAQ inspected.

papers.title: ORL: train a diffusion LM on its own unfinished predictions
papers.full_title: On-Policy Residual Learning for Diffusion Language Models
papers.summary: ORL replays residual predictions encountered by the current model and adds adjacent entropy contraction, training each refinement to resolve uncertainty faster. A specialized runtime turns parallel commitments into lower single-request latency.
papers.change: New October 14 paper; first archive coverage.
papers.evaluation: Qwen-derived 4B model plus LLaDA-2.1-mini and DiffusionGemma. Main suite: GSM8K, MATH-500, HumanEval and MBPP. Author claims up to 6.2x tokens per forward and about 6.9x throughput including dlmrt. Single-request H100 measurements; cross-family literature rows are not scorer-matched.
papers.caveat: The 1,298 versus 746 tokens/s DFlash comparison uses relaxed verification at selected matched accuracy. Strict autoregressive speculation retains accuracy 2.4 points higher. Base/ORL comparisons include selected decoders; throughput is not a universal model-only gain or a lossless guarantee.
papers.access: MIT training/evaluation repository and separate DLMRT runtime are public. Reproducing paper training requires its included Triton kernel; integration of newer kernels remains in progress. Checkpoints and execution not verified.
papers.creator_implication: Relevant to interactive local assistants and editing agents where one request blocks the next; bulk serving remains a different workload.
papers.review_depth: Primary method, benchmark accounting and official repository; no execution

papers.title: Kandinsky S2V: compressed visual memory for speech-driven avatars
papers.full_title: Kandinsky S2V 1.0: Audio-Driven Avatar Video Generation
papers.summary: 2B and 21B models combine image, speech and text with three-scale visual history. Older frames use coarser tokens; five-second chunks retain a bounded memory. Distilled variants reduce 100 network evaluations to 16.
papers.change: October 13 technical report, first archive coverage. Do not equate the paper date with independently verified checkpoint availability.
papers.evaluation: Author evaluation uses 50 clips each from EMTD, CelebV-HQ and HDTF, plus 80 Russian and about 140 multilingual human-comparison cases. Distilled Pro leads aggregate benchmark ranks; individual metrics and human criteria differ.
papers.caveat: Pro trails HeyGen and LongCat in multilingual visual quality; Lite loses some lip synchronization after distillation. The claimed 5.4x speedup uses eight H100s, resident weights and compilation. Ordinary per-chunk timing differs; not real-time generation.
papers.access: Official paper/project page claim MIT code, checkpoints and Diffusers integration. Linked GitHub and model retrieval failed, so downloadable availability and licensing were not independently verified.
papers.creator_implication: A candidate for speech-driven character shots and dubbing research, with lip-sync quality assessed separately from image quality and identity.
papers.review_depth: Primary architecture, runtime and evaluation sections plus project page; no execution
